title: fix(objectql): skipAutomations never skips the builtin audit stamps
body:
Fixes #22070
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`ExecutionContext.skipAutomations` skips the lifecycle hooks bound from metadata. Its own description says it "must never bypass security or audit", and so does the engine's comment at the skip. ObjectQL's builtin audit stamps (`sys_stamp_audit_insert` / `sys_stamp_audit_update`) were registered through the hook binder, which puts `meta` on every registration. `meta` is exactly what the engine's skip keys on, so the opt-out skipped the audit stamps along with the app's hooks.

- `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`, `registerAuditHooks`: every `sys:audit` builtin is now registered in code with `ql.registerHook(event, wrapDeclarativeHook(h, h.handler, { logger, metrics: ql.getHookMetricsRecorder() }), { object, priority, packageId: 'sys:audit' })` and no `meta`, after `unregisterHooksByPackage('sys:audit')`.
  - It uses the same wrapper and the same metrics recorder that `bindHooks` reads at bind time. AppPlugin installs the Server-Timing `hooks` feed in its `init`, ahead of this `start`, so that span keeps counting the builtins.
  - The unregister-by-package keeps a second ObjectQLPlugin on a shared engine idempotent. The constructor accepts an existing `ql`.
  - So the opt-out is the only thing that changes for a builtin. Priority and package id are unchanged.
- `packages/objectql/src/hook-binder.ts`: the comment that called `meta` inert ("The engine ignores unknown options today; this is forward-only") now says what `meta` is: the binding the opt-out keys on.
- `engine.ts` is unchanged. Its one rule stays "`meta` means bound from metadata", and no dispatch site gains a second criterion. The rejected alternative was exempting `sys:audit` at the engine's two dispatch sites. It would add a magic package id to every dispatch site, and it contradicts the spec text "bound from metadata (`bindHooksToEngine`) are skipped".
- `.changeset/22070-audit-stamp-under-skip-automations.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` patch.

## Measurement: which stamped column is lost under the flag

The door is the import runner: `runImport`, then `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, then the engine, then driver-sql on SQLite, with a session user and an organization. Base is `3d9188502e`.

| column | automations on (base) | automations off (base) | automations off (head) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `created_by` | written | **lost** (NULL) | written |
| `updated_by`, insert and update | written | **lost** (NULL) | written |
| a declared plain `tenant_id` field | written | **lost** (NULL) | written |
| `created_at`, `updated_at` | written | written (driver-sql stamps them) | written |
| `organization_id`, or a declared `tenancy.tenantField` (the wall column) | written | written, by the driver from `DriverOptions.tenantId` | written |

- The tenancy wall held throughout. Triage kept p2 on this measurement (6040619736).
- The head column was read with the same probe after this change (the same probe at head `5da266a319`, after a workspace rebuild: `Tests 4 passed (4)`; with automations off the app hook still does not run).
- On a driver that stamps nothing (the in-package pin's stub), `created_at` / `updated_at` are lost too at base, and written at head.

## Pins

`packages/objectql/src/audit-stamp-skip-automations.test.ts`. They were committed red at base in `8e0bfab19d`. They boot a real ObjectKernel with ObjectQLPlugin over a store that stamps nothing, so every audit value on a stored row is the hook's.

- **(a)** Under `skipAutomations` with a session user, an insert stamps `created_by`, `updated_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at` and the declared `tenant_id`. An update stamps `updated_by` and `updated_at`. The answers are the same as without the flag.
- **(b)** Control: a metadata-bound app hook (`bindHooks`, `packageId: 'test-app'`) is still skipped under the flag, and runs without it.
- **(c)** The import door: `runImport` with `runAutomations: false`, through the real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`, stamps the session user on the row it creates and on the row it updates.
- **(d)** Every `sys:audit` entry on the engine carries no `meta`, so a builtin added to the list later cannot reach the opt-out.

## Acceptance notes

- **`plugin.ts` `tenant_id` reading (not changed here; a read-only inference):** `record.tenant_id = record.tenant_id ?? session.organizationId` keeps a caller-supplied `tenant_id` with no flag.
  - That is the client-preferred shape that #15964 and #16311 removed for `created_at` / `created_by`.
  - Not measured. No shipped object declares a plain `tenant_id` the hook stamps: the one shipped `tenant_id` field, `sys_audit_log`'s, is stamped by plugin-audit's writer.
- **For the services lane: `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/claim-seed-ownership.ts` lines 69 to 72 become stale with this change.**
  - It says: "ObjectQL's own `sys_stamp_audit_*` builtins are bound through the hook binder, so they carry metadata and are skipped as well; for this write that changes nothing — the claim has no user to stamp into `updated_by`, and the drivers stamp `updated_at` themselves."
  - Proposed replacement: "ObjectQL's own `sys_stamp_audit_*` builtins are registered in code too (#22070), so they also run on every claimed row; for this write they stamp `updated_at` only, because the claim has no user to stamp into `updated_by`."
  - Left out of this PR on the seat's instruction. No change to #22067's code.
- **#22067's `reown`:** on driver-sql, its `updated_at` was already written under the flag (the driver stamps it). It carries no `session.userId`, so it writes no `updated_by` before or after this change.
- **H2:** the two stamps are the only platform builtins that carried `meta`. The binder's other callers are metadata sources: `plugin.ts` metadata-service binding and hook reload, and `runtime` app artifacts. No `registerHook` call under `packages/` passes `meta`.
